summary: RBAC cache rekey failure blocks just-in-time role escalation for console/runbook actions
description:
Issue summary:

Users requesting just-in-time (JIT) RBAC escalations via the internal runbook/console are intermittently blocked. The identity proxy returns a 403 for the ephemeral role token even though Okta shows the user in the approving group and the approval workflow completed successfully. This appears correlated with a background RBAC cache rekey operation that runs hourly.

Impact:
- ~12% of JIT role elevation requests fail during the hourly rekey window for affected hosts.
- Oncall engineers cannot elevate to runbook executor role; blocks incident remediation for impacted services.
- Visible increase in support tickets and PagerDuty alerts during rekey windows.

Observed by reporter during a live incident at 2026-03-09 16:22 UTC.
impact: Oncall/runbook role elevation failures during rekey windows; immediate operational impact on incident remediation workflows; increased support load.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Ensure user is member of 'oncall-runbooks-approvers' group in Okta and JIT approval flow is active.
2) Trigger an approval for 'runbook-executor' via internal console while RBAC cache rekey job is scheduled to run (every hour on the hour).
3) Observe identity-proxy logs and runbook service response; many requests return 403 with 'ephemeral token not found' or 'role assertion mismatch'.
4) Retry >30s after rekey job completes — request succeeds in most cases.
5) Repeat during different rekey windows to confirm intermittent pattern.
Note: reproduces reliably when request overlaps with rekey job start time + ~45s.
Relevant services: identity-proxy v2.8.1, rbac-cache-worker v1.3.0, runbook-api v4.2.0.
observed_behavior: Identity proxy rejects ephemeral role token assertions during RBAC rekey job with 403 and log entries referencing missing cache key. Approvals show as completed in approval queue but token binding does not appear in the cache store for ~30-90s.
expected_behavior: JIT approvals should succeed immediately after approver action and remain resilient to background cache rekey operations; no 403s should be returned if Okta approval completed successfully and token binding exists.
logs: 2026-03-09T16:22:11Z identity-proxy [req-id=3b7e2c] WARNING: ephemeral token binding not found for user=lucas.rivera@redwood.ai, attempt=1
2026-03-09T16:22:12Z runbook-api [req-id=3b7e2d] ERROR: role-assertion-failed status=403 reason='rbac cache key missing' approval_id=apr-84210
2026-03-09T16:22:18Z rbac-cache-worker [job=hourly-rekey] INFO: started rekey run cycle uid=rekey-20260309-16
2026-03-09T16:23:05Z rbac-cache-worker [job=hourly-rekey] INFO: finished rekey run cycle duration=47s affected_keys=1.2k
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: rekey job deletes and rebuilds the cache in-place, creating a small window where token bindings are temporarily unavailable.
Hypothesis B: a race between token binding write and cache rekey worker causes loss of newly-bound keys when writes occur just before rekey compaction.
Initial findings: identity-proxy attempts a lookup in in-memory cache and, on miss, does NOT fall back to persistent store; missing fallback path introduced in v2.8.1 refactor.
Observed that rbac-cache-worker logs show compact/delete patterns rather than atomic swap; rekey job does: iterate keys -> delete -> repopulate. This creates a non-zero window of key absence.
Proof point: when we disabled rekey job on one staging shard and re-ran test requests overlapping the shard's previous rekey window, failures stopped for that shard.
comments: Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-09T17:04Z: Noted spike in support tickets and PagerDuty paged twice during rekey window. Captured sample req-ids and approval IDs. Escalating to SRE for cache behavior review.
SRE (Diego Martinez) 2026-03-09T18:10Z: Confirmed rekey worker pattern is delete-then-repopulate across all prod shards. Opening engineering bug for safe-swap algorithm. Assigned INT-220220.
Eng (Mei Chen) 2026-03-10T09:32Z: Found a change in in-memory lookup logic in identity-proxy v2.8.1 that removed fallback to datastore on cache miss. Rolling back that change to test.
SRE (Diego Martinez) 2026-03-10T11:05Z: Temporary mitigation applied: stagger rekey jobs by shard (delay window) to avoid cross-shard bulk deletions. Monitoring for reduced failure rate.
Reporter (Lucas Rivera) 2026-03-10T12:20Z: Verified that after staggered rollout, my JIT elevation works consistently in the next hourly window. Will continue to monitor.
Eng (Mei Chen) 2026-03-11T08:50Z: Proposed fix: change rekey worker to use write-to-new-keyspace-then-atomic-rename (safe-swap). Also re-enable datastore fallback in identity-proxy. Preparing PRs.
SRE (Diego Martinez) 2026-03-12T14:12Z: PRs merged to staging; integration tests covering race windows added to CI. Preparing rollout plan to prod with immediate mitigation still in place.
resolution: Mitigation: staggered rekey schedule deployed to prod shards to avoid wide simultaneous delete windows. Permanent fix merged: rbac-cache-worker now populates a new keyspace and performs atomic swap; identity-proxy restored persistent-store fallback for cache misses. Monitoring shows failure rate reduced to <0.1% during rekey windows. Rollout notes: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h. Follow-up: add synthetic JIT elevation tests to hourly rekey CI job and add SLA alert if failure rate >1% during rekey windows.
